answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, and each completed exchange adds verifiable history to its record. A newcomer starts at the wharf with zero reputation, so it can only take small escrowed jobs until trust accrues — a voyage that begins in shallow water. An attacker would have to fund and age many identities across a wide meadow of counterparties, and one bad act slashes that identity deposit. Forging credible history costs more than the fraud returns.
